clue.text: Perhaps I changed colour

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that they have undergone a change of complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of PERHAPS I. The surface makes 'colour' look like part of the speaker's change, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphire is a deep blue shade, named after the gemstone, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Second time for philosopher

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A philosopher gets a second chance at life.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise person, the traditional figure of a philosopher.

clue.text: Two accepted level is about one

indicators.note: is about tells us the accepted level surrounds the next piece

parts.note: par is the accepted or normal level, as in 'up to par'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Two people agree on a standard that is roughly one.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text reads 'The', which cannot be a definition; the clue needs 'Two'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is a set of two things, so the number two is its synonym.

clue.text: If tooth is aching, you can settle matter for good

definitions.text: If tooth is aching, you can
definitions.meaning: with a painful tooth you can get the dentist to pull it
to resolve a dispute once and for all by open confrontation

explanation.surface: Dental advice doubles as advice for ending a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to extract something such as a tooth, and also to confront a dispute until it is settled.

clue.text: Nuts and some drinks — a lot of ness follows

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Nuts and some drinks — a lot of ness follows': ROUND (some drinks) is clear but 'a lot of ness' cannot give THE BEND; the text is garbled and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Nuts and some drinks — a lot of ness follows

clue.text: Snatch forty winks, as well as turning in

indicators.note: in tells us the turned piece goes inside the nap word

parts.note: kip is British slang for a short sleep, like forty winks

indicators.note: turning tells us the word for 'as well as' is written backwards

parts.note: and means as well as

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a quick doze while also rolling over in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' turns 'as well as' into DNA. 'Snatch' looks like part of the nap ('snatch forty winks') but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to abduct or seize a person, which is what snatch means here.

clue.text: Leaden container that's hidden

indicators.note: hidden tells us the answer lies inside the words container that's

explanation.surface: A heavy lead box has been put out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across contaINER That's.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden in the figurative sense means sluggish and lifeless, the same as inert.

clue.text: A revolution in each canton? That won't happen

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismisses talk of an uprising in every Swiss canton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A revolution in' rearranges the letters of EACH CANTON. Swiss cantons make the uprising sound political, but 'revolution' is only the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal or prediction meaning something is impossible or will never occur.

clue.text: Irishman is Ireland's rising suppl tarts

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Irishman is Ireland's rising suppl tarts': the wordplay PAT + IS + EIRE'S reversed is clear, but the definition is cut short at 'suppl' and no source gives the printed words.
annotationWithheld.clue: Irishman is Ireland's rising suppl tarts

clue.text: Ours give out -—- it's very serious

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sounds the alarm that our side is giving out, and it is no joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of OURS GIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievous describes harm or wrong that is severe, as in grievous bodily harm, so it means very serious.

clue.text: Go away and indulge in rumpy-pumpy

definitions.meaning: rumpy-pumpy is jokey British slang for sex

explanation.surface: A couple are told to clear off and get on with their romping.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word it is the brush-off; split as BE AT IT it is the slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for leaving at once, and when split into three words means to be engaged in sex.

clue.text: Wally if near the bar becomes fluid

indicators.note: becoming fluid means losing shape, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool, standing close to the pub counter, starts to get unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes fluid' rearranges IF NEAR THE BAR. 'Wally' is British slang for a silly person, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wally is British slang for a foolish person, which is a synonym of a scatterbrained featherbrain.

clue.text: Falsifies marks? Nonsense!

parts.note: to fiddle accounts is to falsify them
ticks are marks made on a page

explanation.surface: A teacher accused of doctoring grades dismisses the charge as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old-fashioned exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.

clue.text: Roofing pig pushed around

indicators.note: around tells us the word for pushed surrounds the pig

parts.note: barged means pushed roughly
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A pig is shoved about on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: A bargeboard runs along the sloping gable edge of a roof, which is why 'Roofing' can define it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargeboard is a board fixed along a gable edge of a roof, so it is a piece of roofing.

clue.text: First drink's swallowed, in a state

indicators.note: swallowed tells us the drink takes in the other piece

parts.note: a draught is a drink or gulp
1ST, written IST in letters, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Someone who downed their first drink is now worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on drink's is a link meaning 'has'. 'In a state' is British for agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state means being very upset, which is what distraught means.

clue.text: It's' morning, and I leave my friend

parts.note: taken as written
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone announces it is morning and they are off, saying goodbye to their pal.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe in 'It's'' is a printing slip; it changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used in English as a matey way of saying 'my friend'.

clue.text: Among the 2 that failed, notice list of winners

indicators.note: among tells us the notice goes inside the rearranged letters
failed suggests the words fell apart, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 2 means the answer at 2 down, a couple, with the article in front of it
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: From the two who flopped, someone spots a ranking of the successful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that failed' scrambles THE with the 2-down answer to give HITPARE, and 'Among' places the notice inside. A cross-referenced answer used as anagram fodder is a Times convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit parade is a chart of the best-selling records, a list of the winners in popularity.

clue.text: Suitably equipped, Bill tried to win right out of order

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: out of order says the right letter is taken from its place and put back elsewhere

parts.note: courted means tried to win someone's affection

explanation.surface: A man named Bill made an improper attempt to win, though he was properly kitted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' shifts the right letter one place later, after the T. 'Bill' looks like a name; it is an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutred means dressed or fitted out with the proper gear, so suitably equipped.

clue.text: Find somewhere to eat that's accessible

definitions.meaning: to secure a place at a restaurant
able to be got at or reached

explanation.surface: Booking a restaurant table also means it is easy to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as GET A TABLE it is a restaurant booking; as GET-AT-ABLE it means reachable.
explanation.definitionFit: Getatable is an informal word for reachable, built from 'get at' and the suffix 'able'.

clue.text: Caught first part of play, "Prickly Pears" perhaps

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Act I is the opening section of a play

explanation.surface: Someone saw only the opening act of a play called Prickly Pears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prickly Pears' looks like a play title but defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Prickly pears are a kind of cactus, so they are examples of cacti.

clue.text: Livid when musicians cover up shortfall and spend recklessly

indicators.note: cover up tells us the musicians surround the shortfall

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
a lack is a shortfall
to blue money is old British slang for squandering it

explanation.surface: Someone is furious when the band hides a deficit and blows the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Livid' reads as angry, but the definition uses its older sense of bruised and discoloured.
explanation.definitionFit: Livid originally means bluish and discoloured, like a bruise, which is what black-and-blue describes.

clue.text: Marsupial loses 24 halfway across plateau

indicators.note: loses tells us the marsupial has some letters taken away

parts.note: a kangaroo is a marsupial

indicators.note: halfway across takes only the first half of the 24 answer

parts.note: 24 points to the answer at 24 across, a rabbit

explanation.surface: An animal loses something halfway across a high plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halfway across' gives ANG, the first half of the 24-across answer, and 'loses' removes it from KANGAROO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Karoo is a semi-desert tableland in South Africa, a high plateau region.

clue.text: Constituent having to catch up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a trap is a device to catch

explanation.surface: A voter is obliged to catch up with events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TRAP; 'having to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A part is a component of a whole, which is a constituent.

clue.text: Film director in a rush

definitions.meaning: Carol ..., British director of The Third Man
a tall waterside plant like a rush

explanation.surface: A director of films is in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol Reed directed The Third Man, and a reed is a marsh plant similar to a rush.

clue.text: Rabbit new in the marketplace

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for new goes inside the marketplace

parts.note: the agora was the marketplace of an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: A rabbit newly appears at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside AGORA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a breed of rabbit prized for its long silky wool.

clue.text: Aunt Sally, for instance, is a person open to criticism

definitions.meaning: Aunt Sally is a British fairground and pub game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head
someone it is acceptable to attack or mock

explanation.surface: A traditional target figure is also someone fit to be attacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground game, and also a figurative name for an easy target.
explanation.definitionFit: A game played at a fair is literally a fair game, and the idiom means a legitimate target for attack.

clue.text: Carried a gun around, getting in the way

indicators.note: around tells us the word for carried a gun is turned back to front

parts.note: ported in the military sense means held a rifle diagonally across the body

explanation.surface: A gunman walking about makes a nuisance of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses PORTED, as in the drill order 'port arms'.
explanation.definitionFit: De trop is French borrowed into English for unwanted or superfluous, so a person getting in the way.

clue.text: In the original version, Teddy's included in football team

indicators.note: included in says the short name goes inside the team

parts.note: United is a common football club name, such as Manchester United
Ted is short for Teddy; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: In the first cut of the story, Teddy joins the football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts TED inside UNITED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedited material has not been changed by an editor, so it remains in its original form.
